questionText:
The corners and mid-points of the sides of a triangle are named using the distinct letters P, Q, R, S, T and U, but not necessarily in the same order. Consider the following statements:

• The line joining P and R is parallel to the line joining Q and S.
• P is placed on the side opposite to the corner T.
• S and U cannot be placed on the same side.

Which one of the following statements is correct based on the above information?
options: P cannot be placed at a corner
S cannot be placed at a corner
U cannot be placed at a mid-point
R cannot be placed at a corner
explanation:
Step 1: Understand the positions on a triangle
A triangle has 3 corner points (vertices) and 3 mid-points on its sides, giving a total of 6 positions for $P, Q, R, S, T, U$.

Step 2: Analyze parallel line segments
In a triangle, two line segments formed by these 6 points can only be parallel if one segment connects two mid-points (a mid-segment) and the other segment lies along the base side opposite to that mid-segment.

Step 3: Analyze constraints on $S$
Since the line joining $P$ and $R$ is parallel to the line joining $Q$ and $S$, one pair must consist of two mid-points and the other pair must lie on the base side.
If $S$ were at a corner, it would lie on a side. But given the conditions that $S$ and $U$ cannot be on the same side and $P$ is opposite to corner $T$, placing $S$ at a corner leads to a contradiction in placing the remaining points without violating side-exclusivity.

Therefore, S cannot be placed at a corner (it must be at a mid-point).
